name: Wildermieming
kurzbeschreibung: Charming hamlet in the Mieminger Plateau, featuring the wild and romantic Stuibenfall waterfall and breathtaking views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The idyllic mountain municipality of Wildermieming is situated at an altitude of 872 metres above sea level on the eastern Mieming Plateau within Tyrol's Innsbruck-Land district, nestling at the foot of the dramatic Mieming Range beneath the Hohe Munde (2,662 m). Home to approximately 1,000 residents, this peaceful village rests on a gentle glacial moraine knoll above the Upper Inn Valley. The Mieming Plateau is renowned as the sunniest high plateau in North Tyrol, celebrated for its expansive larch meadows that transform into a sea of radiant golden yellow each autumn. Wildermieming achieved international renown as the original filming location for the television series 'Der Bergdoktor' (The Mountain Doctor). The community offers village tranquillity, mountain huts, championship golf, and panoramic trails set against limestone peaks.

Geschichte

Traces of human settlement on the Mieming Plateau date back to the Bronze and Iron Ages, as the elevated corridor formed a prehistoric travel route linking the Inn Valley with the Fernpass. In classical antiquity, the area belonged to the Roman province of Raetia. Wildermieming was first documented in 1352 in a charter that simultaneously recorded the local village church. Granted in 1976, the municipal coat of arms displays a golden mountain pine branch on a green background, honouring the essential protective role played by dwarf pine forests in shielding the settlement from avalanches descending from the Hohe Munde. The village captured international hearts between 1992 and 1997 as the fictional setting 'Sonnenstein' for the popular television series 'Der Bergdoktor', with an authentic farmhouse in the hamlet of Afers serving as the doctor's practice. The parish church of Saint Nicholas was rebuilt in Baroque style in 1655.

Anreise

Wildermieming offers effortless accessibility coupled with scenic alpine approaches. Motorists leave the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Telfs-West junction and ascend along the Mieminger federal road B189 to reach Wildermieming in roughly six kilometres. Arriving from southern Germany, toll-free access is available via Garmisch-Partenkirchen and Mittenwald to Telfs or via Füssen across the Fernpass highway B179 through Nassereith. Rail passengers arrive at nearby Telfs-Pfaffenhofen railway station on the Arlberg line, served frequently by regional express trains and the S-Bahn Tirol. From the railway station, regular VVT bus route 4176 connects directly to Wildermieming village centre and the hamlet of Afers.

Tipps

A favourite destination for television enthusiasts is the historic 'Bergdoktorhaus' in the hamlet of Afers: this timber farmstead served as the surgery and home of television doctor Thomas Burgner and offers panoramic views towards the Stubai Alps. Hikers should traverse the picturesque Ochsenbründl trail up to the family-run Neue Alplhütte (1,504 m) nestled below the Hohe Wand, renowned for Tyrolean cheese dumplings and Kaiserschmarrn pancakes. Golfers can play at the neighbouring 27-hole Golfpark Mieminger Plateau, among the finest golf courses in the Eastern Alps. In autumn, the radiant golden larch woods provide peaceful strolling, while winter invites guests to explore cross-country ski trails and winter walking routes.
